{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FmJmFUFo74ypju5iCKYCfE","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n2\t\n3\tResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\n4\tstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n5\t`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n6\t\n7\tEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\n8\trule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\n9\tnames a concrete type.\n10\t\"\"\"\n11\t\n12\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n13\t\n14\timport re\n15\tfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\n16\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n17\t\n18\tfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\n19\tfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n20\t\n21\tTAB_STOP = 4\n22\tSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n23\t\n24\t# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n25\t# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\n26\tStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n27\t# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n28\t# when it returns True.\n29\tContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n30\t# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\n31\tAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n32\t# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\n33\tFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n34\t\n35\t\n36\tdef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n37\t    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n38\t    if char == \"\\t\":\n39\t        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n40\t    return col + 1\n41\t\n42\t\n43\tdef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n44\t    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n45\t    end = pos\n46\t    end_col = col\n47\t    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n48\t        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n49\t        end += 1\n50\t    return end_col - col\n51\t\n52\t\n53\tclass Cursor:\n54\t    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n55\t\n56\t    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n57\t        self.line = line\n58\t        self.pos = 0\n59\t        self.col = 0\n60\t        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n61\t        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n62\t        self.in_tab = False\n63\t        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n64\t        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n65\t        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n66\t\n67\t    @property\n68\t    def rest(self) -> str:\n69\t        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n70\t\n71\t        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n72\t        \"\"\"\n73\t        if self.in_tab:\n74\t            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n75\t            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n76\t        return self.line[self.pos :]\n77\t\n78\t    @property\n79\t    def indent(self) -> int:\n80\t        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n81\t        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n82\t\n83\t    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n84\t        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n85\t        end = self.pos\n86\t        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n87\t            end += 1\n88\t        return end\n89\t\n90\t    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n91\t        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n92\t        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n93\t\n94\t    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n95\t        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n96\t        while self.pos < index:\n97\t            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n98\t            self.pos += 1\n99\t            self.in_tab = False\n100\t\n101\t    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n102\t        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n103\t        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n104\t\n105\t    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n106\t        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n107\t\n108\t        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n109\t        \"\"\"\n110\t        target = self.col + columns\n111\t        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n112\t            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n113\t            self.pos += 1\n114\t            self.in_tab = False\n115\t\n116\t    def consume_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n117\t        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed, without overshooting.\n118\t\n119\t        A tab that straddles the target column is split: the cursor stops inside it, and the columns it\n120\t        has left are read back through `rest` as spaces.\n121\t        \"\"\"\n122\t        target = self.col + columns\n123\t        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n124\t            end_col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n125\t            if end_col > target:\n126\t                self.col = target\n127\t                self.in_tab = True\n128\t                return\n129\t            self.col = end_col\n130\t            self.pos += 1\n131\t            self.in_tab = False\n132\t\n133\t\n134\tclass Block:\n135\t    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n136\t\n137\t    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n138\t        self.kind = kind\n139\t        self.parent: Block | None = None\n140\t        self.children: list[Block] = []\n141\t        self.is_open = True\n142\t        self.lines: list[str] = []\n143\t        self.content = \"\"\n144\t        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n145\t        self.level = 0\n146\t        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n147\t        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n148\t        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n149\t        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n150\t        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n151\t        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n152\t\n153\t    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n154\t        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n155\t        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n156\t            return self.children[-1]\n157\t        return None\n158\t\n159\t\n160\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n161\tclass BlockType:\n162\t    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n163\t\n164\t    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n165\t    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n166\t    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n167\t    \"\"\"\n168\t\n169\t    name: str\n170\t    continues: ContinueRule\n171\t    is_container: bool = False\n172\t    accepts_lines: bool = False\n173\t    interruptible: bool = False\n174\t    lazy: bool = False\n175\t    start: StartRule | None = None\n176\t    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n177\t    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n178\t\n179\t    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n180\t        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n181\t            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n182\t        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n183\t            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n184\t\n185\t\n186\tdef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n187\t    return True\n188\t\n189\t\n190\tdef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n191\t    return not cursor.is_blank()\n192\t\n193\t\n194\tdef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n195\t    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n196\t    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n197\t\n198\t\n199\tdef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n200\t    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n201\t\n202\t    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n203\t    \"\"\"\n204\t    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n205\t    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n206\t    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n207\t        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n208\t\n209\t\n210\tdef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n211\t    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n212\t    root = block\n213\t    while root.parent is not None:\n214\t        root = root.parent\n215\t    assert root.references is not None\n216\t    return root.references\n217\t\n218\t\n219\tdef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n220\t    return False\n221\t\n222\t\n223\tTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\n224\tTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n225\t\n226\t\n227\tdef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n228\t    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n229\t\n230\t    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n231\t    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n232\t    \"\"\"\n233\t    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n234\t        return None\n235\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n236\t    line = cursor.line\n237\t    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n238\t        return None\n239\t    marker = line[start]\n240\t    count = 0\n241\t    for char in line[start:]:\n242\t        if char == marker:\n243\t            count += 1\n244\t        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n245\t            return None\n246\t    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n247\t        return None\n248\t    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n249\t    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n250\t\n251\t\n252\tATX_MARKER = \"#\"\n253\tATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n254\t\n255\t\n256\tdef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n257\t    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n258\t\n259\t    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n260\t    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n261\t    \"\"\"\n262\t    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n263\t        return None\n264\t    line = cursor.line\n265\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n266\t    end = start\n267\t    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n268\t        end += 1\n269\t    level = end - start\n270\t    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n271\t        return None\n272\t    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n273\t        return None\n274\t    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n275\t    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n276\t    heading.level = level\n277\t    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n278\t    return heading\n279\t\n280\t\n281\tdef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n282\t    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n283\t\n284\t    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n285\t    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n286\t    \"\"\"\n287\t    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n288\t    if stripped == content:\n289\t        return content\n290\t    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n291\t        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n292\t    return content\n293\t\n294\t\n295\tSETEXT_MAX_INDENT = 3\n296\tSETEXT_LEVELS = {\"=\": 1, \"-\": 2}\n297\t\n298\t\n299\tdef _setext_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n300\t    \"\"\"Turn the open paragraph into a setext heading when the line is an underline of `=` or `-`.\n301\t\n302\t    The underline has up to three spaces of indentation, one run of a single marker character and\n303\t    only trailing spaces or tabs after it. It applies to the whole paragraph, so every paragraph line\n304\t    becomes heading content. Definitions at the start of the paragraph are extracted first; if nothing\n305\t    is left, the line is not an underline and the paragraph keeps it as text.\n306\t    \"\"\"\n307\t    if container.kind is not PARAGRAPH or cursor.indent > SETEXT_MAX_INDENT:\n308\t        return None\n309\t    line = cursor.line\n310\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n311\t    marker = line[start : start + 1]\n312\t    if marker not in SETEXT_LEVELS:\n313\t        return None\n314\t    underline = line[start:].rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n315\t    if underline.count(marker) != len(underline):\n316\t        return None\n317\t    text = \"\\n\".join(container.lines).strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n318\t    content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(container))\n319\t    if not content:\n320\t        return None\n321\t    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n322\t    # The paragraph's text now lives in the heading. Clearing its lines lets the paragraph close\n323\t    # empty, so it leaves the tree and the heading takes its place.\n324\t    container.lines = []\n325\t    heading = Block(SETEXT_HEADING)\n326\t    heading.level = SETEXT_LEVELS[marker]\n327\t    heading.content = content\n328\t    return heading\n329\t\n330\t\n331\tDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\n332\tPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n333\t    \"paragraph\",\n334\t    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n335\t    accepts_lines=True,\n336\t    interruptible=True,\n337\t    lazy=True,\n338\t    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n339\t    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n340\t)\n341\t# A setext heading is a complete block made from the open paragraph. Its content is parsed as inlines\n342\t# when the document is rendered, like an ATX heading.\n343\tSETEXT_HEADING = BlockType(\n344\t    \"setext_heading\",\n345\t    continues=_never_continues,\n346\t    start=_setext_heading_start,\n347\t)\n348\t# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n349\t# as soon as the next line arrives.\n350\tTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n351\t    \"thematic_break\",\n352\t    continues=_never_continues,\n353\t    start=_thematic_break_start,\n354\t)\n355\t# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n356\t# inlines when the document is rendered.\n357\tATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n358\t    \"atx_heading\",\n359\t    continues=_never_continues,\n360\t    start=_atx_heading_start,\n361\t)\n362\t\n363\t\n364\tCODE_INDENT = 4\n365\t\n366\t\n367\tdef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n368\t    \"\"\"Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.\n369\t\n370\t    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and\n371\t    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph. The same holds\n372\t    for a lazy continuation of a paragraph that an unmatched container holds.\n373\t    \"\"\"\n374\t    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.lazy_paragraph or cursor.is_blank():\n375\t        return None\n376\t    if cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n377\t        return None\n378\t    cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n379\t    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n380\t\n381\t\n382\tdef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n383\t    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n384\t\n385\t    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n386\t    \"\"\"\n387\t    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n388\t        cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n389\t        return True\n390\t    return False\n391\t\n392\t\n393\tdef _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n394\t    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns.\"\"\"\n395\t    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n396\t\n397\t\n398\tdef _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n399\t    \"\"\"Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n400\t    lines = list(block.lines)\n401\t    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):\n402\t        lines.pop()\n403\t    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in lines)\n404\t\n405\t\n406\t# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n407\t# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.\n408\tINDENTED_CODE = BlockType(\n409\t    \"indented_code\",\n410\t    continues=_indented_code_continues,\n411\t    accepts_lines=True,\n412\t    start=_indented_code_start,\n413\t    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,\n414\t    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,\n415\t)\n416\t\n417\t\n418\tFENCE_CHARS = \"`~\"\n419\tFENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3\n420\tBACKTICK = \"`\"\n421\t\n422\t\n423\t@dataclass\n424\tclass Fence:\n425\t    \"\"\"The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.\n426\t\n427\t    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from\n428\t    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True\n429\t    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing\n430\t    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.\n431\t    \"\"\"\n432\t\n433\t    char: str\n434\t    length: int\n435\t    indent: int\n436\t    language: str\n437\t    opening: bool = True\n438\t    closed: bool = False\n439\t\n440\t\n441\tdef _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:\n442\t    \"\"\"Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`.\"\"\"\n443\t    end = start\n444\t    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:\n445\t        end += 1\n446\t    return end\n447\t\n448\t\n449\tdef _language(info: str) -> str:\n450\t    \"\"\"The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or \"\".\"\"\"\n451\t    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()\n452\t    return words[0] if words else \"\"\n453\t\n454\t\n455\tdef _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n456\t    \"\"\"Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.\n457\t\n458\t    The fence may be indented up to three columns. The info string is the rest of the line, trimmed.\n459\t    A backtick fence whose info string holds a backtick is not a fence, so the line is left to the\n460\t    paragraph, where the backticks form a code span.\n461\t    \"\"\"\n462\t    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n463\t        return None\n464\t    line = cursor.line\n465\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n466\t    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in FENCE_CHARS:\n467\t        return None\n468\t    char = line[start]\n469\t    end = _run_end(line, start, char)\n470\t    if end - start < FENCE_MIN_LENGTH:\n471\t        return None\n472\t    info = line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n473\t    if char == BACKTICK and BACKTICK in info:\n474\t        return None\n475\t    fence = Fence(char=char, length=end - start, indent=cursor.indent, language=_language(info))\n476\t    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n477\t    block = Block(FENCED_CODE)\n478\t    block.fence = fence\n479\t    return block\n480\t\n481\t\n482\tdef _is_closing_fence(cursor: Cursor, fence: Fence) -> bool:\n483\t    \"\"\"True when the line is a closing fence for `fence`.\n484\t\n485\t    It uses the same character, is at least as long as the opening fence, is indented up to three\n486\t    columns, and is followed only by spaces or tabs.\n487\t    \"\"\"\n488\t    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n489\t        return False\n490\t    line = cursor.line\n491\t    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n492\t    end = _run_end(line, start, fence.char)\n493\t    return end - start >= fence.length and not line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n494\t\n495\t\n496\tdef _fenced_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n497\t    \"\"\"Every line continues the block except one after a closing fence.\n498\t\n499\t    A matching closing fence is consumed here and marked. Any other line loses up to the opening\n500\t    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.\n501\t    \"\"\"\n502\t    fence = block.fence\n503\t    assert fence is not None\n504\t    if fence.closed:\n505\t        return False\n506\t    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):\n507\t        fence.closed = True\n508\t        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n509\t        return True\n510\t    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)\n511\t    return True\n512\t\n513\t\n514\tdef _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n515\t    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of a content line. The opening and closing fence lines add nothing.\"\"\"\n516\t    fence = block.fence\n517\t    assert fence is not None\n518\t    if fence.opening:\n519\t        fence.opening = False\n520\t        return\n521\t    if fence.closed:\n522\t        return\n523\t    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n524\t\n525\t\n526\tdef _fenced_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n527\t    \"\"\"Join the content lines, each with a line ending, as the content.\n528\t\n529\t    An unclosed block keeps every line up to the end of its container.\n530\t    \"\"\"\n531\t    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in block.lines)\n532\t\n533\t\n534\t# A fenced code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n535\t# while it is open. It can interrupt a paragraph, because its start rule is tried in the paragraph's\n536\t# container.\n537\tFENCED_CODE = BlockType(\n538\t    \"fenced_code\",\n539\t    continues=_fenced_code_continues,\n540\t    accepts_lines=True,\n541\t    start=_fenced_code_start,\n542\t    add_line=_fenced_code_add_line,\n543\t    finalize=_fenced_code_finalize,\n544\t)\n545\t\n546\t\n547\tHTML_TAG_NAME = r\"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9\\-]*\"\n548\tHTML_ATTRIBUTE = (\n549\t    r\"[ \\t]+[A-Za-z_:][A-Za-z0-9_.:\\-]*\"\n550\t    r\"(?:[ \\t]*=[ \\t]*(?:[^\\\"'=<>`\\x00-\\x20]+|'[^']*'|\\\"[^\\\"]*\\\"))?\"\n551\t)\n552\t# A complete open tag or closing tag, with its name captured, as the raw HTML grammar defines it. Only\n553\t# spaces and tabs may follow it on the line.\n554\tCOMPLETE_OPEN_TAG = re.compile(rf\"<({HTML_TAG_NAME})(?:{HTML_ATTRIBUTE})*[ \\t]*/?>[ \\t]*\")\n555\tCOMPLETE_CLOSE_TAG = re.compile(rf\"</({HTML_TAG_NAME})[ \\t]*>[ \\t]*\")\n556\t# Start condition 1 names. Type 7 excludes them, because type 1 owns them.\n557\tRAW_TEXT_TAG_NAMES = frozenset((\"pre\", \"script\", \"style\", \"textarea\"))\n558\tRAW_TEXT_START = re.compile(r\"<(?:pre|script|style|textarea)(?=[ \\t>]|$)\", re.IGNORECASE)\n559\tRAW_TEXT_END = re.compile(r\"</(?:pre|script|style|textarea)>\", re.IGNORECASE)\n560\t# Start condition 6 names, matched case-insensitively.\n561\tBLOCK_TAG_NAMES = (\n562\t    \"address\", \"article\", \"aside\", \"base\", \"basefont\", \"blockquote\", \"body\", \"caption\", \"center\",\n563\t    \"col\", \"colgroup\", \"dd\", \"details\", \"dialog\", \"dir\", \"div\", \"dl\", \"dt\", \"fieldset\", \"figcaption\",\n564\t    \"figure\", \"footer\", \"form\", \"frame\", \"frameset\", \"h1\", \"h2\", \"h3\", \"h4\", \"h5\", \"h6\", \"head\",\n565\t    \"header\", \"hr\", \"html\", \"iframe\", \"legend\", \"li\", \"link\", \"main\", \"menu\", \"menuitem\", \"nav\",\n566\t    \"noframes\", \"ol\", \"optgroup\", \"option\", \"p\", \"param\", \"search\", \"section\", \"summary\", \"table\",\n567\t    \"tbody\", \"td\", \"tfoot\", \"th\", \"thead\", \"title\", \"tr\", \"track\", \"ul\",\n568\t)\n569\tBLOCK_TAG_START = re.compile(\n570\t    rf\"</?(?:{'|'.join(BLOCK_TAG_NAMES)})(?=[ \\t]|/?>|$)\", re.IGNORECASE\n571\t)\n572\tDECLARATION_START = re.compile(r\"<![A-Za-z]\")\n573\t\n574\t\n575\tHtmlStart = Callable[[str], bool]\n576\tHtmlEnd = Callable[[str], bool]\n577\t\n578\t\n579\tdef _prefix_test(pattern: re.Pattern[str]) -> HtmlStart:\n580\t    \"\"\"A start test that holds when `pattern` matches at the start of the line text.\"\"\"\n581\t    return lambda text: pattern.match(text) is not None\n582\t\n583\t\n584\tdef _search_test(pattern: re.Pattern[str]) -> HtmlEnd:\n585\t    \"\"\"An end test that holds when `pattern` matches anywhere in the line text.\"\"\"\n586\t    return lambda text: pattern.search(text) is not None\n587\t\n588\t\n589\tdef _contains_test(marker: str) -> HtmlEnd:\n590\t    \"\"\"An end test that holds when `marker` appears anywhere in the line text.\"\"\"\n591\t    return lambda text: marker in text\n592\t\n593\t\n594\tdef _is_complete_tag_line(text: str) -> bool:\n595\t    \"\"\"True when the line text is one complete open or closing tag, then spaces and tabs only.\n596\t\n597\t    The tag name may not be `pre`, `script`, `style` or `textarea`.\n598\t    \"\"\"\n599\t    match = COMPLETE_OPEN_TAG.fullmatch(text) or COMPLETE_CLOSE_TAG.fullmatch(text)\n600\t    if match is None:\n601\t        return False\n602\t    return match.group(1).lower() not in RAW_TEXT_TAG_NAMES\n603\t\n604\t\n605\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n606\tclass HtmlKind:\n607\t    \"\"\"One of the seven HTML block types, given by its start test and end test.\n608\t\n609\t    `ends` is the end test for types 1 to 5, which is checked on each line. It is None for types 6\n610\t    and 7, which end before a blank line. `can_interrupt` is False only for type 7, which cannot\n611\t    start while a paragraph is open.\n612\t    \"\"\"\n613\t\n614\t    starts: HtmlStart\n615\t    ends: HtmlEnd | None\n616\t    can_interrupt: bool = True\n617\t\n618\t\n619\t# The seven HTML block types, in spec order. A line starts the first type whose start test holds.\n620\tHTML_KINDS = (\n621\t    HtmlKind(starts=_prefix_test(RAW_TEXT_START), ends=_search_test(RAW_TEXT_END)),\n622\t    HtmlKind(starts=_prefix_test(re.compile(r\"<!--\")), ends=_contains_test(\"-->\")),\n623\t    HtmlKind(starts=_prefix_test(re.compile(r\"<\\?\")), ends=_contains_test(\"?>\")),\n624\t    HtmlKind(starts=_prefix_test(DECLARATION_START), ends=_contains_test(\">\")),\n625\t    HtmlKind(starts=_prefix_test(re.compile(r\"<!\\[CDATA\\[\")), ends=_contains_test(\"]]>\")),\n626\t    HtmlKind(starts=_prefix_test(BLOCK_TAG_START), ends=None),\n627\t    HtmlKind(starts=_is_complete_tag_line, ends=None, can_interrupt=False),\n628\t)\n629\t\n630\t\n631\t@dataclass\n632\tclass HtmlState:\n633\t    \"\"\"The start condition of an HTML block, and whether its end condition has been met.\n634\t\n635\t    `ended` is set when a line meets the end test of types 1 to 5. The block closes on the line after\n636\t    that line, so the line holding the end condition is kept.\n637\t    \"\"\"\n638\t\n639\t    kind: HtmlKind\n640\t    ended: bool = False\n641\t\n642\t\n643\tdef _html_block_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n644\t    \"\"\"Start an HTML block when the line opens with one of the seven start conditions.\n645\t\n646\t    The line may be indented up to three columns. Type 7 cannot start while a paragraph is open, which\n647\t    is the case when the container takes lines or the line lazily continues the open paragraph.\n648\t    \"\"\"\n649\t    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n650\t        return None\n651\t    text = cursor.rest.lstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n652\t    for kind in HTML_KINDS:\n653\t        if not kind.can_interrupt and (container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.lazy_paragraph):\n654\t            continue\n655\t        if kind.starts(text):\n656\t            block = Block(HTML_BLOCK)\n657\t            block.html = HtmlState(kind=kind)\n658\t            return block\n659\t    return None\n660\t\n661\t\n662\tdef _html_block_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n663\t    \"\"\"Types 1 to 5 continue until their end line. Types 6 and 7 continue until a blank line.\"\"\"\n664\t    state = block.html\n665\t    assert state is not None\n666\t    if state.kind.ends is not None:\n667\t        return not state.ended\n668\t    return not cursor.is_blank()\n669\t\n670\t\n671\tdef _html_block_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n672\t    \"\"\"Keep the whole line, unchanged and unescaped, and note when it meets the end condition.\"\"\"\n673\t    state = block.html\n674\t    assert state is not None\n675\t    line = cursor.rest\n676\t    block.lines.append(line)\n677\t    if state.kind.ends is not None and state.kind.ends(line):\n678\t        state.ended = True\n679\t\n680\t\n681\tdef _html_block_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n682\t    \"\"\"Join the raw lines, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n683\t    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in block.lines)\n684\t\n685\t\n686\t# An HTML block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs while it is\n687\t# open. It can interrupt a paragraph, except for type 7, which the start rule refuses in that case.\n688\tHTML_BLOCK = BlockType(\n689\t    \"html_block\",\n690\t    continues=_html_block_continues,\n691\t    accepts_lines=True,\n692\t    start=_html_block_start,\n693\t    add_line=_html_block_add_line,\n694\t    finalize=_html_block_finalize,\n695\t)\n696\t\n697\t\n698\tBLOCK_QUOTE_MARKER = \">\"\n699\t\n700\t\n701\tdef _consume_block_quote_marker(cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n702\t    \"\"\"Consume a `>` marker with up to three columns of indentation and one optional following column.\n703\t\n704\t    The optional column may be part of a tab, which leaves its remaining columns as content. Returns\n705\t    False and leaves the cursor untouched when the line has no marker.\n706\t    \"\"\"\n707\t    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n708\t        return False\n709\t    marker = cursor.next_nonspace()\n710\t    if marker == len(cursor.line) or cursor.line[marker] != BLOCK_QUOTE_MARKER:\n711\t        return False\n712\t    cursor.advance_to(marker + 1)\n713\t    cursor.consume_columns(1)\n714\t    return True\n715\t\n716\t\n717\tdef _block_quote_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n718\t    \"\"\"A line continues the quote when it has a marker. A line without one is left to the lazy rule.\"\"\"\n719\t    return _consume_block_quote_marker(cursor)\n720\t\n721\t\n722\tdef _block_quote_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n723\t    \"\"\"Start a block quote when the line opens with a `>` marker.\"\"\"\n724\t    if not _consume_block_quote_marker(cursor):\n725\t        return None\n726\t    return Block(BLOCK_QUOTE)\n727\t\n728\t\n729\t# A block quote is a container. A line without a marker still reaches a paragraph inside the quote\n730\t# through the engine's lazy rule, and any other unmatched block closes.\n731\tBLOCK_QUOTE = BlockType(\n732\t    \"block_quote\",\n733\t    continues=_block_quote_continues,\n734\t    is_container=True,\n735\t    start=_block_quote_start,\n736\t)\n737\t\n738\t\n739\tclass BlockRegistry:\n740\t    \"\"\"The block types a parse may use: the document root, the fallback paragraph, and start rules.\n741\t\n742\t    Start rules are tried in registration order. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def consume_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed, without overshooting.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is split: the cursor stops inside it, and the columns it\n        has left are read back through `rest` as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while     self.col = target\n                self.in_tab = True\n                return\n            self.col = end_col\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nSETEXT_MAX_INDENT = 3\nSETEXT_LEVELS = {\"=\": 1, \"-\": 2}\n\n\ndef _setext_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Turn the open paragraph into a setext heading when the line is an underline of `=` or `-`.\n\n    The underline has up to three spaces of indentation, one run of a single marker character and\n    only trailing spaces or tabs after it. Definitions at the start of the paragraph are extracted first; if nothing\n    is left, the line is not an underline and the paragraph keeps it as text.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind is not PARAGRAPH or cursor.indent > SETEXT_MAX_INDENT:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    marker = line[start : start + 1]\n    if marker not in SETEXT_LEVELS:\n        return None\n    underline = line[start:].rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    if underline.count(marker) != len(underline):\n        return None\n    text = \"\\n\".join(container.lines).strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(container))\n    if not content:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    # The paragraph's text now lives in the heading. Clearing its lines lets the paragraph close\n    # empty, so it leaves the tree and the heading takes its place.\n    container.lines = []\n    heading = Block(SETEXT_HEADING)\n    heading.level = SETEXT_LEVELS[marker]\n    heading.content = content\n    return heading\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A setext heading is a complete block made from the open paragraph. Its content is parsed as inlines\n# when the document is rendered, like an ATX heading.\nSETEXT_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"setext_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_setext_heading_start,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n# inlines when the document is rendered.\nATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"atx_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_atx_heading_start,\n)\n\n\nCODE_INDENT = 4\n\n\ndef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.\n\n    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and\n    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph. The same holds\n    for a lazy continuation of a paragraph that an unmatched container holds.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.lazy_paragraph or cursor.is_blank():\n        return None\n    if cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n\n    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns.\"\"\"\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n    lines = list(block.lines)\n    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):\n        lines.pop()\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in lines)\n\n\n# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. It is not interruptible, so no start rule runs\n# while it is open: a non-blank line that is not indented closes it through the continue rule.\nINDENTED_CODE = BlockType(\n    \"indented_code\",\n    continues=_indented_code_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    start=_indented_code_start,\n    add_line=_indented_code_add_line,\n    finalize=_indented_code_finalize,\n)\n\n\nFENCE_CHARS = \"`~\"\nFENCE_MIN_LENGTH = 3\nBACKTICK = \"`\"\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass Fence:\n    \"\"\"The opening fence of a fenced code block, and the state it keeps while the block is open.\n\n    `indent` is the columns of indentation on the opening fence; up to that many are removed from\n    each content line. `language` is the first word of the decoded info string. `opening` is True\n    until the opening line reaches the add-line rule, which skips it. `closed` is set when a closing\n    fence matches; the closing line adds nothing and the block closes on the following line.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    char: str\n    length: int\n    indent: int\n    language: str\n    opening: bool = True\n    closed: bool = False\n\n\ndef _run_end(line: str, start: int, char: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Index just past the run of `char` that begins at `start`.\"\"\"\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == char:\n        end += 1\n    return end\n\n\ndef _language(info: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The first word of the info string after backslash unescape and entity decoding, or \"\".\"\"\"\n    words = unescape_and_decode(info).split()\n    return words[0] if words else \"\"\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a fenced code block when the line opens with three or more backticks or tildes.\n\n    The fence may be indented up to three columns. Any other line loses up to the opening\n    fence's indentation, and the rest reaches the add-line rule.\n    \"\"\"\n    fence = block.fence\n    assert fence is not None\n    if fence.closed:\n        return False\n    if _is_closing_fence(cursor, fence):\n        fence.closed = True\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return True\n    cursor.advance_columns(fence.indent)\n    return True\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of a content line. \\t>]|$)\", re.IGNORECASE)\nRAW_TEXT_END = re.compile(r\"</(?:pre|script|style|textarea)>\", re.IGNORECASE)\n# Start condition 6 names, matched case-insensitively.\nBLOCK_TAG_NAMES = (\n \"iframe\", \"legend\", \"li\", \"link\", \"main\", \"menu\", \"menuitem\", \"nav\",\n    \"noframes\", \"ol\", \"optgroup\", \"option\", \"p\", \"param\", \"search\", \"section\", \"summary\", \"table\",\n    \"tbody\", \"td\", \"tfoot\", \"th\", \"thead\", \"title\", \"tr\", \"track\", \"ul\",\n)\nBLOCK_TAG_START = re.compile(\n    rf\"</?(?:{'|'.join(BLOCK_TAG_NAMES)})(?=[ \\t]|/?>|$)\", re.IGNORECASE\n)\nDECLARATION_START = re.compile(r\"<![A-Za-z]\")\n\n\nHtmlStart = Callable[[str], bool]\nHtmlEnd = Callable[[str], bool]\n\n\ndef _prefix_test(pattern: re.Pattern[str]) -> print(equals.stdout)\n    print(dashes.stdout)\n    assert equals.returncode == 0\n    assert dashes.returncode == 0\n    assert equals.stdout.count(\"<h1>\") == 1\n    assert {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01R7uzxaT27kHhnvmzMZ2Cjz","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"HTML rendering.\n\nResponsibility: turn the parsed tree into HTML, escape HTML text and attributes, and\npercent-encode URLs. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return _render_children(root, parse_inline)\n\n\ndef _render_children(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in block.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"block_quote\":\n        return f\"<blockquote>\\n{_render_children(block, parse_inline)}</blockquote>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name in (\"atx_heading\", \"setext_heading\"):\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":\n        return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":\n        return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"html_block\":\n        # Raw lines pass through unchanged. The content already ends with a line ending.\n        return block.content\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    language = block.fence.language\n    if not language:\n        return \"<code>\"\n    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'\n\"\"\"mdparser: a CommonMark 0.31.2 parser delivered as the stdin-to-stdout `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe package uses only the Python standard library. Its phase-1 block structure and phase-2\ninline structure live in the modules below.\n\"\"\"\ncommit 9a6d5fab59d1fe53203bd3d9101b70381fd14ce1\nAuthor: Ed Barlow <edward.m.barlow@gmail.com>\nDate: The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return _render_children(root, parse_inline)\n\n\ndef _render_children(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in block.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"block_quote\":\n        return f\"<blockquote>\\n{_render_children(block, parse_inline)}</blockquote>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name in (\"atx_heading\", \"setext_heading\"):\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":\n        return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":\n        return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"html_block\":\n        # Raw lines pass through unchanged. The content already ends with a line ending.\n        return block.content\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    language = block.fence.language\n    if not language:\n        return \"<code>\"\n    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'\n\"\"\"mdparser: a CommonMark 0.31.2 parser delivered as the stdin-to-stdout `commonmark` executable.\n\nThe package uses only the Python standard library. List looseness reads it.\n        self.last_line_blank = False\n","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def consume_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed, without overshooting.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is split: the cursor stops inside it, and the columns it\n        has left are read back through `rest` as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end_col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            if end_col > target:\n                self.col = target\n                self.in_tab = True\n                return\n            self.col = end_col\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nSETEXT_MAX_INDENT = 3\nSETEXT_LEVELS = {\"=\": 1, \"-\": 2}\n\n\ndef _setext_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Turn the open paragraph into a setext heading when the line is an underline of `=` or `-`.\n\n    The underline has up to three spaces of indentation, one run of a single marker character and\n    only trailing spaces or tabs after it. It applies to the whole paragraph, so every paragraph line\n    becomes heading content. Definitions at the start of the paragraph are extracted first; if nothing\n    is left, the line is not an underline and the paragraph keeps it as text.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind is not PARAGRAPH or cursor.indent > SETEXT_MAX_INDENT:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    marker = line[start : start + 1]\n    if marker not in SETEXT_LEVELS:\n        return None\n    underline = line[start:].rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    if underline.count(marker) != len(underline):\n        return None\n    text = \"\\n\".join(container.lines).strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(container))\n    if not content:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    # The paragraph's text now lives in the heading. Clearing its lines lets the paragraph close\n    # empty, so it leaves the tree and the heading takes its place.\n    container.lines = []\n    heading = Block(SETEXT_HEADING)\n    heading.level = SETEXT_LEVELS[marker]\n    heading.content = content\n    return heading\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A setext heading is a complete block made from the open paragraph. Its content is parsed as inlines\n# when the document is rendered, like an ATX heading.\nSETEXT_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"setext_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_setext_heading_start,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n# inlines when the document is rendered.\nATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"atx_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_atx_heading_start,\n)\n\n\nCODE_INDENT = 4\n\n\ndef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.\n\n    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and\n    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph. The same holds\n    for a lazy continuation of a paragraph that an unmatched container holds.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.lazy_paragraph or cursor.is_blank():\n        return None\n    if cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n\n    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns.\"\"\"\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n    lines = list(block.lines)\n    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):\n        lines.pop()\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in lines)\n\n\n# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. The marker must end the line or be followed by a space\n# or tab, so `-foo` and `1.foo` are not items.\nLIST_MARKER = re.compile(r\"(?:([-+*])|([0-9]{1,9})([.)]))(?=[ \\t]|\\Z)\")\nLIST_MAX_SPACING = 4\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass ListItem:\n    \"\"\"The marker of a list item, and the absolute column where its content begins.\n\n    `delimiter` is the bullet character, or the `.` or `)` after a number. Items with the same kind of\n    marker and the same delimiter share a list. `start` is the number of an ordered marker, and 0 for a\n    bullet. `content_column` is the column a continuation line must reach.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    ordered: bool\n    delimiter: str\n    start: int\n    content_column: int\n\n\ndef _list_item_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a list item when the line opens with a bullet or an ordered marker.\n\n    The marker may have up to three columns of indentation. Inside a paragraph, an item may not start\n    with a blank line, and an ordered item must start at 1. One to four spaces after the marker set the\n    content column. Five or more make the content an indented code block, so the content column is one\n    column after the marker.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    match = LIST_MARKER.match(line, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    ordered = match.group(1) is None\n    number = int(match.group(2)) if ordered else 0\n    empty = not line[match.end() :].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines and (empty or (ordered and number != 1)):\n        return None\n    marker_column = cursor.col + cursor.indent\n    width = match.end() - start\n    cursor.advance_to(match.end())\n    if empty:\n        cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n        spacing = 1\n    else:\n        spacing = indent_columns(line, cursor.pos, cursor.col)\n        if spacing > LIST_MAX_SPACING:\n            spacing = 1\n        cursor.consume_columns(spacing)\n    block = Block(LIST_ITEM)\n    block.item = ListItem(\n        ordered=ordered,\n        delimiter=match.group(3) if ordered else match.group(1),\n        start=number,\n        content_column=marker_column + width + spacing,\n    )\n    return block\n\n\ndef _list_item_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line continues an item that has content. Any other line must reach the content column.\n\n    An empty item ends at the first blank line after its marker, so a blank line cannot give it a second.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.is_blank():\n        return bool(block.children)\n    item = block.item\n    assert item is not None\n    needed = item.content_column - cursor.col\n    if cursor.indent < needed:\n        return False\n    cursor.consume_columns(needed)\n    return True\n\n\n# A list item is a container.
