Its start rule runs in any container that can hold a block, so a new item\n# at the same level closes the previous one through the engine. Grouping items into lists happens at\n# render time.\nLIST_ITEM = BlockType(\n    \"list_item\",\n    continues=_list_item_continues,\n    is_container=True,\n    start=_list_item_start,\n)\n","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1085300e-51d0-4820-bfdf-a72abf49582a","uuid":"3c147dc5-6696-4735-bf17-ab4058aa1ba5","timestamp":"2026-10-14T08:11:17.295Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/mdparser/blocks.py","oldString":"DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(BLOCK_QUOTE)\n","newString":"DEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(BLOCK_QUOTE)\n# After thematic break, so `* * *` is a break and never an item.\nDEFAULT_REGISTRY.register(LIST_ITEM)\n","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def consume_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed, without overshooting.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is split: the cursor stops inside it, and the columns it\n        has left are read back through `rest` as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end_col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            if end_col > target:\n                self.col = target\n                self.in_tab = True\n                return\n            self.col = end_col\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n        # The marker and content column of a list item. None for every other block.\n        self.item: ListItem | None = None\n        # True when the last line that reached this block was blank. List looseness reads it.\n        self.last_line_blank = False\n\n    def open_last_child(self) -> Block | None:\n        \"\"\"The last child if it is still open, otherwise None.\"\"\"\n        if self.children and self.children[-1].is_open:\n            return self.children[-1]\n        return None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass BlockType:\n    \"\"\"The rules that define one kind of block.\n\n    `accepts_lines` marks a leaf that takes line text. `interruptible` lets a start rule close such\n    a leaf (a paragraph); a non-interruptible leaf blocks new starts. `lazy` lets a non-matching\n    line join this block as a lazy continuation. `is_container` lets the block hold child blocks.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    continues: ContinueRule\n    is_container: bool = False\n    accepts_lines: bool = False\n    interruptible: bool = False\n    lazy: bool = False\n    start: StartRule | None = None\n    add_line: AddLineRule | None = None\n    finalize: FinalizeRule | None = None\n\n    def __post_init__(self) -> None:\n        if self.accepts_lines and self.add_line is None:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} accepts lines but has no add_line rule\")\n        if self.lazy and not self.accepts_lines:\n            raise ValueError(f\"block type {self.name!r} is lazy but does not accept lines\")\n\n\ndef _always_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n\ndef _paragraph_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return not cursor.is_blank()\n\n\ndef _paragraph_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _paragraph_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move leading link reference definitions into the document map and keep the remaining text.\n\n    A paragraph that holds only definitions leaves the tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = \"\\n\".join(block.lines).strip(\" \\t\")\n    block.content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(block))\n    if not block.content and block.parent is not None:\n        block.parent.children.remove(block)\n\n\ndef _document_references(block: Block) -> ReferenceMap:\n    \"\"\"The reference map of the document root that `block` belongs to.\"\"\"\n    root = block\n    while root.parent is not None:\n        root = root.parent\n    assert root.references is not None\n    return root.references\n\n\ndef _never_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    return False\n\n\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS = \"*-_\"\nTHEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS = 3\n\n\ndef _thematic_break_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start a thematic break when the rest of the line is three or more matching marker characters.\n\n    Spaces and tabs may appear between and after the markers. Any other character, or four or more\n    columns of indentation, means the line is not a thematic break.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    line = cursor.line\n    if start == len(line) or line[start] not in THEMATIC_BREAK_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    marker = line[start]\n    count = 0\n    for char in line[start:]:\n        if char == marker:\n            count += 1\n        elif char not in SPACE_CHARS:\n            return None\n    if count < THEMATIC_BREAK_MIN_MARKERS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    return Block(THEMATIC_BREAK)\n\n\nATX_MARKER = \"#\"\nATX_MAX_LEVEL = 6\n\n\ndef _atx_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an ATX heading when the line opens with one to six `#` characters.\n\n    The opening run must be followed by a space, a tab or the end of the line. The content is the\n    rest of the line, stripped of surrounding spaces and tabs, without a closing sequence.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= 4:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    end = start\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] == ATX_MARKER:\n        end += 1\n    level = end - start\n    if not 1 <= level <= ATX_MAX_LEVEL:\n        return None\n    if end < len(line) and line[end] not in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    heading = Block(ATX_HEADING)\n    heading.level = level\n    heading.content = _strip_closing_sequence(line[end:].strip(SPACE_CHARS))\n    return heading\n\n\ndef _strip_closing_sequence(content: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Remove a closing run of `#` characters from the end of heading content.\n\n    The run must be the whole content or follow a space or tab. So `foo#` keeps its hash, and so\n    does `foo \\\\#`, where the backslash is not whitespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    stripped = content.rstrip(ATX_MARKER)\n    if stripped == content:\n        return content\n    if stripped == \"\" or stripped[-1] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        return stripped.rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    return content\n\n\nSETEXT_MAX_INDENT = 3\nSETEXT_LEVELS = {\"=\": 1, \"-\": 2}\n\n\ndef _setext_heading_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Turn the open paragraph into a setext heading when the line is an underline of `=` or `-`.\n\n    The underline has up to three spaces of indentation, one run of a single marker character and\n    only trailing spaces or tabs after it. It applies to the whole paragraph, so every paragraph line\n    becomes heading content. Definitions at the start of the paragraph are extracted first; if nothing\n    is left, the line is not an underline and the paragraph keeps it as text.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind is not PARAGRAPH or cursor.indent > SETEXT_MAX_INDENT:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    marker = line[start : start + 1]\n    if marker not in SETEXT_LEVELS:\n        return None\n    underline = line[start:].rstrip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    if underline.count(marker) != len(underline):\n        return None\n    text = \"\\n\".join(container.lines).strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    content = extract_definitions(text, _document_references(container))\n    if not content:\n        return None\n    cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n    # The paragraph's text now lives in the heading. Clearing its lines lets the paragraph close\n    # empty, so it leaves the tree and the heading takes its place.\n    container.lines = []\n    heading = Block(SETEXT_HEADING)\n    heading.level = SETEXT_LEVELS[marker]\n    heading.content = content\n    return heading\n\n\nDOCUMENT = BlockType(\"document\", continues=_always_continues, is_container=True)\nPARAGRAPH = BlockType(\n    \"paragraph\",\n    continues=_paragraph_continues,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    interruptible=True,\n    lazy=True,\n    add_line=_paragraph_add_line,\n    finalize=_paragraph_finalize,\n)\n# A setext heading is a complete block made from the open paragraph. Its content is parsed as inlines\n# when the document is rendered, like an ATX heading.\nSETEXT_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"setext_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_setext_heading_start,\n)\n# A thematic break is a complete single-line block. It never takes continuation lines, so it closes\n# as soon as the next line arrives.\nTHEMATIC_BREAK = BlockType(\n    \"thematic_break\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_thematic_break_start,\n)\n# An ATX heading is a complete single-line block, like a thematic break. Its content is parsed as\n# inlines when the document is rendered.\nATX_HEADING = BlockType(\n    \"atx_heading\",\n    continues=_never_continues,\n    start=_atx_heading_start,\n)\n\n\nCODE_INDENT = 4\n\n\ndef _indented_code_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    \"\"\"Start an indented code block when a non-blank line is indented four columns or more.\n\n    A leaf that takes lines as the container means the line would continue an open paragraph, and\n    an indented code block cannot interrupt one, so the line is left to that paragraph. The same holds\n    for a lazy continuation of a paragraph that an unmatched container holds.\n    \"\"\"\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines or cursor.lazy_paragraph or cursor.is_blank():\n        return None\n    if cursor.indent < CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n    return Block(INDENTED_CODE)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line or a line indented four columns or more continues the code block.\n\n    The four columns of indentation are consumed here, so the add-line rule receives the content.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.is_blank() or cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        cursor.consume_columns(CODE_INDENT)\n        return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _indented_code_add_line(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Keep the literal rest of the line, including any indentation beyond the four columns.\"\"\"\n    block.lines.append(cursor.rest)\n\n\ndef _indented_code_finalize(block: Block) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Drop trailing blank lines and join the rest, each with a line ending, as the content.\"\"\"\n    lines = list(block.lines)\n    while lines and not lines[-1].strip(SPACE_CHARS):\n        lines.pop()\n    block.content = \"\".join(line + \"\\n\" for line in lines)\n\n\n# An indented code block is a leaf that takes lines. Add the remaining text to the deepest open block.\n        tip = self._tip()\n        if not all_closed and not cursor.is_blank() and tip.kind.lazy:\n            self._add_line(tip, cursor)\n        else:\n            self._close_below(container)\n            if container.kind.accepts_lines:\n                self._add_line(container, cursor)\n            elif not cursor.is_blank():\n                paragraph = Block(self.registry.fallback)\n                self._attach(paragraph, container)\n                self._add_line(paragraph, cursor)\n        self._record_blankness(container, blank_line)\n","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def consume_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed, without overshooting.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is split: the cursor stops inside it, and the columns it\n        has left are read back through `rest` as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end_col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            if end_col > target:\n                self.col = target\n                self.in_tab = True\n                return\n            self.col = end_col\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Five or more make the content an indented code block, so the content column is one\n    column after the marker.\n    \"\"\"\n    if cursor.indent >= CODE_INDENT:\n        return None\n    line = cursor.line\n    start = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    match = LIST_MARKER.match(line, start)\n    if match is None:\n        return None\n    ordered = match.group(1) is None\n    number = int(match.group(2)) if ordered else 0\n    empty = not line[match.end() :].strip(SPACE_CHARS)\n    if container.kind.accepts_lines and (empty or (ordered and number != 1)):\n        return None\n    marker_column = cursor.col + cursor.indent\n    width = match.end() - start\n    cursor.advance_to(match.end())\n    if empty:\n        cursor.advance_to(len(line))\n        spacing = 1\n    else:\n        spacing = indent_columns(line, cursor.pos, cursor.col)\n        if spacing > LIST_MAX_SPACING:\n            spacing = 1\n        cursor.consume_columns(spacing)\n    block = Block(LIST_ITEM)\n    block.item = ListItem(\n        ordered=ordered,\n        delimiter=match.group(3) if ordered else match.group(1),\n        start=number,\n        content_column=marker_column + width + spacing,\n    )\n    return block\n\n\ndef _list_item_continues(block: Block, cursor: Cursor) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A blank line continues an item that has content. The block that took the line, and each of its ancestors, takes the flag. A blank line in\n        a block quote or a fenced code block is not a gap between blocks, so it does not set the flag.\n        \"\"\"\n        if blank_line and container.children:\n            container.children[-1].last_line_blank = True\n        receiver = self._tip()\n        flag = blank_line and receiver.kind is not BLOCK_QUOTE and receiver.kind is not FENCED_CODE\n        node: Block | None = receiver\n        while node is not None:\n            node.last_line_blank = flag\n            node = node.parent\n\n    def _match_open_blocks(self, cursor: Cursor) -> Block:","originalFile":"\"\"\"Phase 1: block tree, block-type registry, per-line procedure, and lazy continuation.\n\nResponsibility: consume lines one at a time, match them against open blocks, look for new block\nstarts, and add remaining text to the deepest open block. Link reference definitions are handed to\n`mdparser.refs` when a paragraph closes.\n\nEach block type is a `BlockType` record registered in a `BlockRegistry`. A type supplies a start\nrule, a continue rule and a close (finalize) rule; the per-line loop in `DocumentParser` never\nnames a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom mdparser.entities import unescape_and_decode\nfrom mdparser.refs import ReferenceMap, extract_definitions\n\nTAB_STOP = 4\nSPACE_CHARS = \" \\t\"\n\n# A start rule inspects the rest of the line below `container`. It returns a new block, after\n# advancing the cursor past its marker, or None, leaving the cursor untouched.\nStartRule = Callable[[\"Cursor\", \"Block\"], \"Block | None\"]\n# A continue rule decides whether the line continues an open block. It advances the cursor only\n# when it returns True.\nContinueRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], bool]\n# An add-line rule appends the remaining line text to a leaf block that accepts lines.\nAddLineRule = Callable[[\"Block\", \"Cursor\"], None]\n# A finalize rule runs once when a block closes, for example to set its content.\nFinalizeRule = Callable[[\"Block\"], None]\n\n\ndef next_column(char: str, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the column after `char`, which sits at column `col`. Tabs advance to the next tab stop.\"\"\"\n    if char == \"\\t\":\n        return col + TAB_STOP - col % TAB_STOP\n    return col + 1\n\n\ndef indent_columns(line: str, pos: int, col: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Return the width in columns of the spaces and tabs starting at `pos`, which sits at `col`.\"\"\"\n    end = pos\n    end_col = col\n    while end < len(line) and line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n        end_col = next_column(line[end], end_col)\n        end += 1\n    return end_col - col\n\n\nclass Cursor:\n    \"\"\"A position in one source line, tracked both as a character index and as a column.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, line: str) -> None:\n        self.line = line\n        self.pos = 0\n        self.col = 0\n        # True when a container has consumed only part of the tab at `pos`. The columns left in the tab\n        # are content indentation, so `rest` gives them as spaces.\n        self.in_tab = False\n        # True when the line can only join the open paragraph as a lazy continuation. A start rule that\n        # cannot interrupt a paragraph then leaves the line alone.\n        self.lazy_paragraph = False\n\n    @property\n    def rest(self) -> str:\n        \"\"\"The text from the current position to the end of the line.\n\n        When a tab is partly consumed, its remaining columns come first, as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.in_tab:\n            remaining = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col) - self.col\n            return \" \" * remaining + self.line[self.pos + 1 :]\n        return self.line[self.pos :]\n\n    @property\n    def indent(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Columns of indentation from the current position to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        return indent_columns(self.line, self.pos, self.col)\n\n    def next_nonspace(self) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Index of the first character at or after the current position that is not a space or tab.\"\"\"\n        end = self.pos\n        while end < len(self.line) and self.line[end] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end += 1\n        return end\n\n    def is_blank(self) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"True when only spaces and tabs remain on the line.\"\"\"\n        return self.next_nonspace() == len(self.line)\n\n    def advance_to(self, index: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Move the cursor forward to character `index`, tracking the column.\"\"\"\n        while self.pos < index:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def advance_nonspace(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Skip spaces and tabs up to the next non-space character.\"\"\"\n        self.advance_to(self.next_nonspace())\n\n    def advance_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is consumed whole, so the column may overshoot.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            self.col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n    def consume_columns(self, columns: int) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Consume spaces and tabs until `columns` columns are passed, without overshooting.\n\n        A tab that straddles the target column is split: the cursor stops inside it, and the columns it\n        has left are read back through `rest` as spaces.\n        \"\"\"\n        target = self.col + columns\n        while self.pos < len(self.line) and self.col < target and self.line[self.pos] in SPACE_CHARS:\n            end_col = next_column(self.line[self.pos], self.col)\n            if end_col > target:\n                self.col = target\n                self.in_tab = True\n                return\n            self.col = end_col\n            self.pos += 1\n            self.in_tab = False\n\n\nclass Block:\n    \"\"\"A node in the block tree. Leaf blocks keep their raw lines; `content` is set when they close.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, kind: BlockType) -> None:\n        self.kind = kind\n        self.parent: Block | None = None\n        self.children: list[Block] = []\n        self.is_open = True\n        self.lines: list[str] = []\n        self.content = \"\"\n        # Heading level, 1 to 6, for an ATX heading. Zero for every other block.\n        self.level = 0\n        # The document-wide reference map. Only the document root holds one.\n        self.references: ReferenceMap | None = None\n        # The opening fence and its state, for a fenced code block. None for every other block.\n        self.fence: Fence | None = None\n        # The start condition and end state of an HTML block. None for every other block.\n        self.html: HtmlState | None = None\n        # The marker and content column of a list item. None for every other block.\n        self.item: ListItem | None = None\n        # True when the last line that reached this block was blank. A run of list items with the same marker becomes one list.\n\n    In a tight list item a paragraph is its inline content, without a `<p>` wrapper. Each piece ends\n    with a line ending unless it is inline text, so a line ending is added before the next piece.\n    \"\"\"\n    pieces: list[str] = []\n    children = block.children\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(children):\n        child = children[index]\n        if child.kind.name == \"list_item\":\n            end = index + 1\n            while end < len(children) and _same_list(child, children[end]):\n                end += 1\n            pieces.append(_render_list(children[index:end], parse_inline))\n            index = end\n            continue\n        if tight and child.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n            pieces.append(parse_inline(child.content))\n        else:\n            pieces.append(_render_block(child, parse_inline))\n        index += 1\n    html = \"\"\n    for piece in pieces:\n        if html and not html.endswith(\"\\n\"):\n            html += \"\\n\"\n        html += piece\n    return html\n\n\ndef _same_list(first: Block, other: Block) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when `other` is a list item that continues the list `first` starts.\n\n    A change of bullet character or of ordered delimiter starts a new list.\n    \"\"\"\n    if other.kind.name != \"list_item\":\n        return False\n    assert first.item is not None and other.item is not None\n    return (first.item.ordered, first.item.delimiter) == (other.item.ordered, other.item.delimiter)\n\n\ndef _render_list(items: list[Block], parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One `<ul>` or `<ol>` holding an `<li>` per item. An ordered list states its start unless it is 1.\"\"\"\n    first = items[0].item\n    assert first is not None\n    tag = \"ol\" if first.ordered else \"ul\"\n    open_tag = f'<ol start=\"{first.start}\">' if first.ordered and first.start != 1 else f\"<{tag}>\"\n    loose = _list_is_loose(items)\n    body = \"\".join(_render_item(item, loose, parse_inline) for item in items)\n    return f\"{open_tag}\\n{body}</{tag}>\\n\"\n\n\ndef _list_is_loose(items: list[Block]) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A list is loose when a blank line separates two of its items, or two blocks inside one item.\"\"\"\n    for index, item in enumerate(items):\n        has_next_item = index + 1 < len(items)\n        if has_next_item and _ends_with_blank_line(item):\n            return True\n        for child_index, child in enumerate(item.children):\n            has_next_block = child_index + 1 < len(item.children) or has_next_item\n            if has_next_block and _ends_with_blank_line(child):\n                return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _ends_with_blank_line(block: Block) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"True when `block` ends with a blank line, looking into the last child of each list item.\"\"\"\n    node: Block | None = block\n    while node is not None:\n        if node.last_line_blank:\n            return True\n        if node.kind.name != \"list_item\" or not node.children:\n            return False\n        node = node.children[-1]\n    return False\n\n\ndef _render_item(item: Block, loose: bool, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One `<li>`. The conformance runner compares normalized HTML, so tag structure and\nentities must match the spec examples.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport string\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import Block\n\nInlineParser = Callable[[str], str]\n\nESCAPES = ((\"&\", \"&amp;\"), (\"<\", \"&lt;\"), (\">\", \"&gt;\"), ('\"', \"&quot;\"))\nURL_SAFE_CHARS = frozenset(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + \";,/?:@&=+$-_.!~*'()#\")\nHEX_DIGITS = frozenset(string.hexdigits)\n\n\ndef escape_html(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Escape &, <, > and \" so the text renders as literal characters. The ampersand goes first.\"\"\"\n    for raw, entity in ESCAPES:\n        text = text.replace(raw, entity)\n    return text\n\n\ndef percent_encode_url(url: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Percent-encode a URL for use in an attribute.\n\n    URL-safe ASCII and existing %XX escapes are kept. Every other character is encoded as its\n    UTF-8 bytes, so a lone % becomes %25.\n    \"\"\"\n    out: list[str] = []\n    index = 0\n    while index < len(url):\n        char = url[index]\n        if char == \"%\" and _is_hex_pair(url[index + 1 : index + 3]):\n            out.append(url[index : index + 3])\n            index += 3\n            continue\n        if char in URL_SAFE_CHARS:\n            out.append(char)\n        else:\n            out.extend(f\"%{byte:02X}\" for byte in char.encode(\"utf-8\"))\n        index += 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\n\ndef _is_hex_pair(text: str) -> bool:\n    return len(text) == 2 and all(char in HEX_DIGITS for char in text)\n\n\ndef render_document(root: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Phase 2 walk: render the top-level blocks in order, one line ending after each block.\n\n    `parse_inline` is the inline parser hook. It receives the raw content of each paragraph and\n    returns that content's HTML.\n    \"\"\"\n    return _render_children(root, parse_inline)\n\n\ndef _render_children(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in block.children)\n\n\ndef _render_block(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:\n    if block.kind.name == \"block_quote\":\n        return f\"<blockquote>\\n{_render_children(block, parse_inline)}</blockquote>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"paragraph\":\n        return f\"<p>{parse_inline(block.content)}</p>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"thematic_break\":\n        return \"<hr />\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name in (\"atx_heading\", \"setext_heading\"):\n        return f\"<h{block.level}>{parse_inline(block.content)}</h{block.level}>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"indented_code\":\n        return f\"<pre><code>{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"fenced_code\":\n        return f\"<pre>{_fenced_code_open_tag(block)}{escape_html(block.content)}</code></pre>\\n\"\n    if block.kind.name == \"html_block\":\n        # Raw lines pass through unchanged. The content already ends with a line ending.\n        return block.content\n    raise ValueError(f\"no HTML renderer for block type {block.kind.name!r}\")\n\n\ndef _fenced_code_open_tag(block: Block) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The `<code>` opening tag for a fenced block, with a language class when the info string has a word.\"\"\"\n    assert block.fence is not None\n    language = block.fence.language\n    if not language:\n        return \"<code>\"\n    return f'<code class=\"language-{escape_html(language)}\">'\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":61,"oldLines":10,"newStart":61,"newLines":92,"lines":["     return _render_children(root, parse_inline)"," "," ","-def _render_children(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser) -> str:","-    return \"\".join(_render_block(child, parse_inline) for child in block.children)","+def _render_children(block: Block, parse_inline: InlineParser, tight: bool = False) -> str:","+    \"\"\"Render the children in order. Registry tests use block types defined here, which shows that\nthe loop never names a concrete type.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser import blocks\nfrom mdparser.blocks import (\n    DOCUMENT,\n    PARAGRAPH,\n    Block,\n    BlockRegistry,\n    BlockType,\n    Cursor,\n    DocumentParser,\n    indent_columns,\n    next_column,\n    parse_lines,\n)\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_contents(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    return [child.content for child in block.children if child.kind is PARAGRAPH]\n\n\n# --- Column helpers ---\n\n\ndef test_next_column_for_a_space_advances_one() -> None:\n    assert next_column(\" \", 3) == 4\n\n\ndef test_next_column_for_a_tab_advances_to_next_tab_stop() -> None:\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 0) == 4\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 2) == 4\n    assert next_column(\"\\t\", 4) == 8\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_counts_spaces() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"   x\", 0, 0) == 3\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_expands_a_leading_tab_to_four() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\tx\", 0, 0) == 4\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_pads_a_tab_after_spaces_to_the_tab_stop() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"  \\tx\", 0, 0) == 4\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_counts_two_tabs_as_eight() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\t\\tx\", 0, 0) == 8\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_is_zero_without_leading_whitespace() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"x  \", 0, 0) == 0\n\n\ndef test_indent_columns_starts_from_the_given_column() -> None:\n    assert indent_columns(\"\\tx\", 0, 2) == 2\n\n\n# --- Cursor ---\n\n\ndef test_cursor_rest_starts_as_the_whole_line() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"abc\").rest == \"abc\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_is_blank_for_empty_and_whitespace_lines() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"\").is_blank()\n    assert Cursor(\" \\t \").is_blank()\n\n\ndef test_cursor_is_not_blank_with_text() -> None:\n    assert not Cursor(\"  a\").is_blank()\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_nonspace_tracks_column_across_a_tab() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"  \\t x\")\n    cursor.advance_nonspace()\n    assert cursor.pos == 4\n    assert cursor.col == 5\n    assert cursor.rest == \"x\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_columns_consumes_whole_tab_when_it_overshoots() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"\\tx\")\n    cursor.advance_columns(2)\n    assert cursor.pos == 1\n    assert cursor.col == 4\n    assert cursor.rest == \"x\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_columns_stops_at_the_target_column() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"    x\")\n    cursor.advance_columns(2)\n    assert cursor.rest == \"  x\"\n\n\ndef test_cursor_indent_reports_columns_to_next_text() -> None:\n    assert Cursor(\"\\t\\tx\").indent == 8\n\n\ndef test_cursor_advance_to_moves_by_characters() -> None:\n    cursor = Cursor(\"abc\")\n    cursor.advance_to(2)\n    assert cursor.rest == \"c\"\n\n\n# --- Empty and blank input ---\n\n\ndef test_empty_input_gives_empty_document() -> None:\n    assert parse_lines([]).children == []\n\n\ndef test_one_empty_line_gives_empty_document() -> None:\n    assert parse_lines([\"\"]).children == []\n\n\ndef test_blank_lines_only_give_empty_document() -> None:\n    assert parse_lines([\"\", \"  \", \"\\t\", \" \\t \"]).children == []\n\n\ndef test_leading_and_trailing_blank_lines_add_no_blocks() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"\", \" \", \"word\", \"\", \"\\t\", \"\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"word\"]\n\n\n# --- Paragraphs ---\n\n\ndef test_single_line_makes_one_paragraph() -> None:\n    root = test_continuation_lines_drop_their_leading_indentation() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"first\", \"      second\", \"\\tthird\"])\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == test_paragraph_is_closed_when_document_ends() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"word\"])\n    assert all(not child.is_open for child in root.children)\n    assert not root.is_open\n\n\ndef False]\n\n\ndef test_document_root_is_a_container_with_no_content() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"a\"])\n    assert root.kind is DOCUMENT\n    assert root.content == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_paragraph_raw_lines_are_recorded_as_read() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"one\", \"   two\"])\n    assert root.children[0].lines == [\"one\", \"two\"]\n\n\ndef _shape(root: Block) -> test_default_registry_start_rules_are_setext_thematic_break_atx_heading_indented_fenced_html_and_block_quote() -> None:\n    assert blocks.DEFAULT_REGISTRY.starts() == (\n        blocks.SETEXT_HEADING,\n        blocks.THEMATIC_BREAK,\n        blocks.ATX_HEADING,\n        blocks.INDENTED_CODE,\n        blocks.FENCED_CODE,\n        blocks.HTML_BLOCK,\n        blocks.BLOCK_QUOTE,\n    )\n\n\ndef test_lazy_block_type_must_accept_lines() -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        BlockType(\"bad\", continues=lambda block, cursor: True, lazy=True)\n\n\ndef test_leaf_block_type_must_have_an_add_line_rule() -> None:\n    with pytest.raises(ValueError):\n        BlockType(\"bad\", continues=lambda block, cursor: True, accepts_lines=True)\n\n\n# --- Extensibility: block types registered without changing the loop ---\n\n\ndef _rule_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    if cursor.rest.strip(\" \\t\") == \"***\":\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return Block(RULE)\n    return None\n\n\nRULE = BlockType(\"rule\", continues=lambda block, cursor: False, start=_rule_start)\n\n\ndef test_registered_start_rule_interrupts_a_paragraph() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"a\", \"***\", \"b\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"paragraph\", \"rule\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root) == [\"a\", \"b\"]\n\n\ndef test_registered_start_rule_closes_an_unmatched_block_before_it_starts() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"***\", \"b\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"rule\", \"paragraph\"]\n    assert root.children[0].is_open is False\n\n\ndef _raw_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    if cursor.rest.startswith(\"<<\"):\n        cursor.advance_to(len(cursor.line))\n        return Block(RAW)\n    return None\n\n\nRAW = BlockType(\n    \"raw\",\n    continues=lambda block, cursor: True,\n    accepts_lines=True,\n    add_line=lambda block, cursor: block.lines.append(cursor.rest),\n    start=_raw_start,\n)\n\n\ndef test_start_rule_is_not_tried_inside_a_non_interruptible_leaf() -> None:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(RAW)\n    registry.register(RULE)\n    root = parse_lines([\"<<\", \"***\"], registry)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"raw\"]\n    assert root.children[0].lines[-1] == \"***\"\n\n\n# --- Lazy paragraph continuation, via a test-only container return True\n    return False\n\n\ndef _quote_start(cursor: Cursor, container: Block) -> Block | None:\n    index = cursor.next_nonspace()\n    if cursor.line[index : index + 1] == \">\":\n        cursor.advance_to(index + 1)\n        return Block(QUOTE)\n    return None\n\n\nQUOTE = BlockType(\"quote\", continues=_quote_continues, is_container=True, start=_quote_start)\n\n\ndef quote_registry() -> BlockRegistry:\n    registry = BlockRegistry(root=DOCUMENT, fallback=PARAGRAPH)\n    registry.register(QUOTE)\n    return registry\n\n\ndef test_quote_holds_its_paragraph() ->  assert kinds(root) == [\"quote\"]\n    assert paragraph_contents(root.children[0]) == [\"a\\nb\"]\n\n\ndef test_blank_line_ends_the_lazy_continuation() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"> a\", {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1nuRGHbzHjrbjfHEfoz","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_018bq5Wt3mB1Tk2QBC13CCuq","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_list_items.py","content":"\"\"\"List item tests: the seven declared checks from FEATURE-List-Items.md, then block-tree and exact-output\ntests for markers, content columns, empty items, start numbers, laziness and interruption.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import DEFAULT_REGISTRY, LIST_ITEM, PARAGRAPH, Block, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the child block types of `block`, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_texts(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Raw content of every paragraph under `block`, in document order.\"\"\"\n    texts: list[str] = []\n    for child in block.children:\n        if child.kind is PARAGRAPH:\n            texts.append(child.content)\n        texts.extend(paragraph_texts(child))\n    return texts\n\n\ndef only_item(lines: list[str]) -> Block:\n    \"\"\"The single list item at the top of the document built from `lines`.\"\"\"\n    root = parse_lines(lines)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"list_item\"]\n    return root.children[0]\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-List-Items.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_items_bullet_items(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Each bullet marker line starts one li element, and consecutive items of one marker form one ul.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    items = [\"first\", \"second\", \"third\"]\n    source = \"\".join(\"- \" + text + \"\\n\" for text in items)\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == len(items)\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<ul>\") == 1\n    for text in items:\n        assert text in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_items_ordered_start_number(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An ordered list takes its start number from the first item, and ten digits is not a marker.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    number = 123456789\n    good = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=str(number) + \". ok\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    bad = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=str(number) + \"0. not ok\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(good.stdout)\n    print(bad.stdout)\n    assert good.returncode == 0\n    assert bad.returncode == 0\n    assert ('start=\"' + str(number) + '\"') in good.stdout\n    assert bad.stdout.count(\"<ol\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_items_continuation_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A continuation paragraph indented to the content column joins the item, giving a loose item with two paragraphs.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- one\\n\\n  two\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_items_insufficient_indent_ends_item(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A paragraph indented less than the content column is outside the item.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- one\\n\\n two\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_items_empty_items(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Empty items are allowed in the middle of a list, but an empty item cannot interrupt a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    middle = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- foo\\n-\\n- bar\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    interrupt = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"foo\\n*\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(middle.stdout)\n    print(interrupt.stdout)\n    assert middle.returncode == 0\n    assert interrupt.returncode == 0\n    assert middle.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 2 + 1\n    assert interrupt.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_items_nested_and_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A sublist indented to the content column nests, and a code block six spaces in is code inside the item.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    nested = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- foo\\n  - bar\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    code = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- foo\\n\\n      bar\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(nested.stdout)\n    print(code.stdout)\n    assert nested.returncode == 0\n    assert code.returncode == 0\n    assert nested.stdout.count(\"<ul>\") == 2\n    assert code.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_items_four_spaces_is_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A marker indented four spaces is code, not a list item.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"    1.  A paragraph\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<ol\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Markers ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"bullet\", [\"-\", \"+\", \"*\"])\ndef test_each_bullet_character_starts_an_item(bullet: str) -> None:\n    item = only_item([f\"{bullet} foo\"])\n    assert item.item is not None\n    assert item.item.ordered is False\n    assert item.item.delimiter == bullet\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"delimiter\", [\".\", \")\"])\ndef test_ordered_marker_records_its_number_and_delimiter(delimiter: str) -> None:\n    item = only_item([f\"3{delimiter} foo\"])\n    assert item.item is not None\n    assert item.item.ordered is True\n    assert item.item.start == 3\n    assert item.item.delimiter == delimiter\n\n\ndef test_nine_digit_number_is_a_marker() -> None:\n    item = only_item([\"123456789. foo\"])\n    assert item.item is test_marker_may_be_indented_three_spaces() -> None:\n    item = only_item([\"   - foo\"])\n    assert item.item is not None\n\n\ndef test_marker_indented_four_spaces_is_indented_code() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"    - foo\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"indented_code\"]\n\n\ndef test_thematic_break_takes_precedence_over_an_item() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"* * *\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"thematic_break\"]\n\n\ndef test_item_is_a_container_for_blocks() -> None:\n    assert LIST_ITEM.is_container is True\n\n\ndef test_default_registry_includes_list_item() ->    assert item.item.content_column == 4\n\n\ndef test_five_spaces_after_marker_make_the_content_code() -> None:\n    item = only_item([\"-     foo\"])\n    assert item.item is not None\n    assert item.item.content_column == 2\n    assert kinds(item) == [\"indented_code\"]\n\n\ndef test_blank_start_content_column_is_marker_plus_one() -> None:\n    item = only_item([\"1.\"])\n    assert    item = only_item([\"-\"])\n    assert item.children == []\n\n\ndef test_empty_item_takes_an_indented_continuation_line() -> None:\n    item = only_item([\"-\", \"  foo\"])\n    assert kinds(item) bad.stdout.count(\"<ol\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_items_continuation_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A continuation paragraph indented to the content column joins the item, giving a loose (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1085300e-51d0-4820-bfdf-a72abf49582a","uuid":"3df10160-97d9-4fbb-8eac-a5e8e45c4466","timestamp":"2026-10-14T08:12:24.882Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/CommonMark/runs/20261014.053711/build/commonmark/tests/test_list_items.py","oldString":"def test_two_blank_lines_end_an_item_with_content() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"- foo\", \"\", \"\", \"  bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"list_item\", \"paragraph\"]","newString":"def test_blank_lines_inside_an_item_with_content_do_not_end_it() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"- foo\", \"\", \"\", \"  bar\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"list_item\"]\n    assert paragraph_texts(root) == [\"foo\", \"bar\"]","originalFile":"\"\"\"List item tests: the seven declared checks from FEATURE-List-Items.md, then block-tree and exact-output\ntests for markers, content columns, empty items, start numbers, laziness and interruption.\n\nThe declared checks are transcribed first, with their assertions unchanged. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import DEFAULT_REGISTRY, LIST_ITEM, PARAGRAPH, Block, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the child block types of `block`, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_texts(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Raw content of every paragraph under `block`, in document order.\"\"\"\n    texts: list[str] = []\n    for child in block.children:\n        if child.kind is PARAGRAPH:\n            texts.append(child.content)\n        texts.extend(paragraph_texts(child))\n    return texts\n\n\ndef only_item(lines: list[str]) -> Block:\n    \"\"\"The single list item at the top of the document built from `lines`.\"\"\"\n    root = parse_lines(lines)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"list_item\"]\n    return root.children[0]\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-List-Items.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_items_bullet_items(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Each bullet marker line starts one li element, and consecutive items of one marker form one ul.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    items = [\"first\", \"second\", \"third\"]\n    source = \"\".join(\"- \" + text + \"\\n\" for text in items)\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == len(items)\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<ul>\") == 1\n    for text in items:\n        assert text in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_items_ordered_start_number(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An ordered list takes its start number from the first item, and ten digits is not a marker.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    number = 123456789\n    good = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=str(number) + \". ok\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    bad = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=str(number) + \"0. not ok\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(good.stdout)\n    print(bad.stdout)\n    assert good.returncode == 0\n    assert bad.returncode == 0\n    assert ('start=\"' + str(number) + '\"') in good.stdout\n    assert bad.stdout.count(\"<ol\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_items_continuation_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A continuation paragraph indented to the content column joins the item, giving a loose item with two paragraphs.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- one\\n\\n  two\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_items_insufficient_indent_ends_item(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A paragraph indented less than the content column is outside the item.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- one\\n\\n two\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_items_empty_items(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Empty items are allowed in the middle of a list, but an empty item cannot interrupt a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    middle = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- foo\\n-\\n- bar\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    interrupt = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"foo\\n*\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(middle.stdout)\n    print(interrupt.stdout)\n    assert middle.returncode == 0\n    assert interrupt.returncode == 0\n    assert middle.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 2 + 1\n    assert interrupt.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_items_nested_and_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A sublist indented to the content column nests, and a code block six spaces in is code inside the item.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    nested = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- foo\\n  - bar\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    code = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- foo\\n\\n      bar\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(nested.stdout)\n    print(code.stdout)\n    assert nested.returncode == 0\n    assert code.returncode == 0\n    assert nested.stdout.count(\"<ul>\") == 2\n    assert code.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_items_four_spaces_is_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A marker indented four spaces is code, not a list item.\"\"\"\n    import subprocess\n\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"    1. The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import DEFAULT_REGISTRY, LIST_ITEM, PARAGRAPH, Block, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the child block types of `block`, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_texts(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Raw content of every paragraph under `block`, in document order.\"\"\"\n    texts: list[str] = []\n    for child in block.children:\n        if child.kind is PARAGRAPH:\n            texts.append(child.content)\n        texts.extend(paragraph_texts(child))\n    return texts\n\n\ndef only_item(lines: list[str]) -> Block:\n    \"\"\"The single list item at the top of the document built from `lines`.\"\"\"\n    root = parse_lines(lines)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"list_item\"]\n    return root.children[0]\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-List-Items.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_items_bullet_items(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Each bullet marker line starts one li element, and consecutive items of one marker form one ul.\"\"\"\n    items = [\"first\", \"second\", \"third\"]\n    source = \"\".join(\"- \" + text + \"\\n\" for text in items)\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == len(items)\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<ul>\") == 1\n    for text in items:\n        assert text in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_items_ordered_start_number(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An ordered list takes its start number from the first item, and ten digits is not a marker.\"\"\"\n    number = 123456789\n    good = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=str(number) + \". ok\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    bad = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=str(number) + \"0. not ok\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(good.stdout)\n    print(bad.stdout)\n    assert good.returncode == 0\n    assert bad.returncode == 0\n    assert ('start=\"' + str(number) + '\"') in good.stdout\n    assert bad.stdout.count(\"<ol\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_items_continuation_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A continuation paragraph indented to the content column joins the item, giving a loose item with two paragraphs.\"\"\"\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- one\\n\\n  two\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_items_insufficient_indent_ends_item(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A paragraph indented less than the content column is outside the item.\"\"\"\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- one\\n\\n two\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_items_empty_items(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Empty items are allowed in the middle of a list, but an empty item cannot interrupt a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    middle = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- foo\\n-\\n- bar\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    interrupt = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"foo\\n*\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(middle.stdout)\n    print(interrupt.stdout)\n    assert middle.returncode == 0\n    assert interrupt.returncode == 0\n    assert middle.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 2 + 1\n    assert interrupt.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_items_nested_and_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A sublist indented to the content column nests, and a code block six spaces in is code inside the item.\"\"\"\n    nested = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- foo\\n  - bar\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    code = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- foo\\n\\n      bar\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(nested.stdout)\n    print(code.stdout)\n    assert nested.returncode == 0\n    assert code.returncode == 0\n    assert nested.stdout.count(\"<ul>\") == 2\n    assert code.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_items_four_spaces_is_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A marker indented four spaces is code, not a list item.\"\"\"\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"    1.  A paragraph\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<ol\") == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<pre>\") == 1\n\n\n# --- Markers ---\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"bullet\", [\"-\", \"+\", \"*\"])\ndef test_each_bullet_character_starts_an_item(bullet: str) -> None:\n    item = only_item([f\"{bullet} foo\"])\n    assert item.item is not None\n    assert item.item.ordered is False\n    assert item.item.delimiter == bullet\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"delimiter\", [\".\", \")\"])\ndef test_ordered_marker_records_its_number_and_delimiter(delimiter: str) -> None:\n    item = only_item([f\"3{delimiter} foo\"])\n    assert item.item is not None\n    assert item.item.ordered is True\n    assert item.item.start == 3\n    assert item.item.delimiter == delimiter\n\n\ndef test_nine_digit_number_is_a_marker() -> None:\n    item = only_item([\"123456789. foo\"])\n    assert item.item is not None\n    assert item.item.start == 123456789\n\n\ndef test_ten_digit_number_is_not_a_marker() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"1234567890. foo\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == root = parse_lines([\"    - foo\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"indented_code\"]\n\n\ndef test_thematic_break_takes_precedence_over_an_item() -> None:\n    root = parse_lines([\"* * *\"])\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"thematic_break\"]\n\n\ndef test_item_is_a_container_for_blocks() -> None:\n    assert LIST_ITEM.is_container is True\n\n\ndef test_default_registry_includes_list_item() ->    assert item.item.content_column == 4\n\n\ndef test_five_spaces_after_marker_make_the_content_code() -> None:\n    item = only_item([\"-     foo\"])\n    assert item.item is not None\n    assert item.item is not None\n    assert item.item.content_column == 3\n\n\ndef test_content_column_is_absolute_for_a_nested_item() -> None:\n    outer = only_item([\"- - foo\"])\n    inner = The rest act on the\nblock tree returned by `parse_lines` and on the exact stdout bytes, which is the state handed back.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom mdparser.blocks import DEFAULT_REGISTRY, LIST_ITEM, PARAGRAPH, Block, parse_lines\n\n\ndef run_commonmark(project_root: Path, source: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:\n    return subprocess.run(\n        [str(project_root / \"commonmark\")],\n        input=source,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        cwd=project_root,\n        check=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef kinds(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Names of the child block types of `block`, in order.\"\"\"\n    return [child.kind.name for child in block.children]\n\n\ndef paragraph_texts(block: Block) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Raw content of every paragraph under `block`, in document order.\"\"\"\n    texts: list[str] = []\n    for child in block.children:\n        if child.kind is PARAGRAPH:\n            texts.append(child.content)\n        texts.extend(paragraph_texts(child))\n    return texts\n\n\ndef only_item(lines: list[str]) -> Block:\n    \"\"\"The single list item at the top of the document built from `lines`.\"\"\"\n    root = parse_lines(lines)\n    assert kinds(root) == [\"list_item\"]\n    return root.children[0]\n\n\n# --- Declared acceptance checks (transcribed from FEATURE-List-Items.md) ---\n\n\ndef test_items_bullet_items(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Each bullet marker line starts one li element, and consecutive items of one marker form one ul.\"\"\"\n    items = [\"first\", \"second\", \"third\"]\n    source = \"\".join(\"- \" + text + \"\\n\" for text in items)\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=source, capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == len(items)\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<ul>\") == 1\n    for text in items:\n        assert text in result.stdout\n\n\ndef test_items_ordered_start_number(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An ordered list takes its start number from the first item, and ten digits is not a marker.\"\"\"\n    number = 123456789\n    good = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=str(number) + \". ok\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    bad = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=str(number) + \"0. not ok\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(good.stdout)\n    print(bad.stdout)\n    assert good.returncode == 0\n    assert bad.returncode == 0\n    assert ('start=\"' + str(number) + '\"') in good.stdout\n    assert bad.stdout.count(\"<ol\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_items_continuation_paragraph(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A continuation paragraph indented to the content column joins the item, giving a loose item with two paragraphs.\"\"\"\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- one\\n\\n  two\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 2\n\n\ndef test_items_insufficient_indent_ends_item(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A paragraph indented less than the content column is outside the item.\"\"\"\n    result = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- one\\n\\n two\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(result.stdout)\n    assert result.returncode == 0\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 1\n    assert result.stdout.count(\"<p>\") == 1\n\n\ndef test_items_empty_items(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Empty items are allowed in the middle of a list, but an empty item cannot interrupt a paragraph.\"\"\"\n    middle = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"- foo\\n-\\n- bar\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    interrupt = subprocess.run([str(project_root / \"commonmark\")], input=\"foo\\n*\\n\", capture_output=True, text=True)\n    print(middle.stdout)\n    print(interrupt.stdout)\n    assert middle.returncode == 0\n    assert interrupt.returncode == 0\n    assert middle.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 2 + 1\n    assert interrupt.stdout.count(\"<li>\") == 0\n\n\ndef test_items_nested_and_code(project_root: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A sublist indented to the content column nests, and a code block six spaces in is code
